selected_evidence.requirement: Snapshot-recoverable /srv/data set up and populated with data
selected_evidence.summary: Built a loopback btrfs filesystem, created 'current' subvolume, mounted it at /srv/data via fstab, and populated it with app data, recording baseline checksums.

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline filesystem snapshot captured before modification
selected_evidence.summary: Created read-only btrfs snapshot 'snap_baseline' of the current subvolume, confirmed via subvolume list and directory listing.
Overwrote config.txt with corrupted content, deleted file1.txt, and added a stray junk file, with listing/content proof.

selected_evidence.requirement: Exact restore of snapshot content after modification
selected_evidence.summary: Performed subvolume-swap rollback to snap_baseline and verified restored files match original sha256 checksums exactly (all OK), stray file gone, corrupted content reverted.

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + data health)
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 88feca03-aee0-475e-8197-2863fc8b7651 plus verified mounted /srv/data and checksum-OK data prior to reboot.
Issued sudo reboot in background; connection closed by remote host confirms the reboot command was accepted and executed before disconnecting.
Immediate poll attempt shows connection refused, confirming the node was actually down mid-reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
selected_evidence.summary: Exec access restored with new boot_id 6523512c-7e09-44bf-a9c7-4ff3135ac8b5, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual reboot occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required data and filesystem mount
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed /srv/data remounted via fstab post-reboot with identical file listing and identical sha256 checksums to the pre-modification baseline.
Listed btrfs subvolumes after reboot showing current, snap_baseline, and corrupted-history subvolumes all intact for continued recoverability.
